questions.text: Service learning is best described as education that:
questions.explanation: Service learning is education in action which places a lot of emphasis on building communities through service, making learning and entrepreneurship come alive.
options: Takes place exclusively in the classroom
Places emphasis on building communities through service while making learning come alive
Only benefits the community, not the students

questions.text: Which of the following best defines service learning?
questions.explanation: Service learning is a method of teaching that combines formal instruction with related service in the community.
options: A method of teaching that combines formal instruction with related service in the community
A punishment assigned by school management
A method of assessing student performance

questions.text: Service learning helps students develop Knowledge, Skills and Abilities (KSAs) to deal effectively with:
questions.explanation: Service learning integrates service and academic learning to promote understanding of course content while helping students develop KSAs to deal effectively with complex social issues and problems.

questions.text: According to the American Association for Higher Education, service learning is coordinated by an institution of higher education and the community to:
questions.explanation: According to the AAHE, service learning is coordinated to help foster civic responsibilities and is integrated to enhance the academic curriculum of enrolled students.
options: Help foster civic responsibilities and enhance the academic curriculum

questions.text: The core principles of service learning are:
questions.explanation: The core principles of service learning are: engagement, reflection, reciprocity and public dissemination.
options: Engagement, reflection, reciprocity and public dissemination
Planning, execution, monitoring and evaluation only

questions.text: Service learning is regarded as a type of:
questions.explanation: Service learning is regarded as an experimental/experiential education that integrates meaningful community service with instruction and reflection.

questions.text: The phrase 'experience enhances understanding; understanding leads to more effective action' best describes:
questions.explanation: In service learning, 'experience enhances understanding: understanding leads to more effective action' — describing the dynamic learning process.

questions.text: Service learning may address complex issues such as:
questions.explanation: Service learning may address complex issues like disability awareness, cultural diversity, child abuse, child trafficking, drug abuse, community partnerships, etc.
options: Disability awareness, cultural diversity, child abuse, drug abuse and community partnerships

questions.text: Which of the following is a characteristic of well-planned service learning experiences?
questions.explanation: A well-planned service learning experience is positive, meaningful and real to the participants.
options: They are competitive rather than cooperative
They address simplified problems in isolation
They are positive, meaningful and real to the participants

questions.text: Service learning promotes which type of experiences?
questions.explanation: Service learning experiences involve cooperative rather than competitive experiences and promote skills associated with teamwork, community involvement and citizenship.
options: Cooperative rather than competitive experiences, promoting teamwork and citizenship
One-sided experiences that only benefit students

questions.text: Service learning addresses problems in:
questions.explanation: Service learning addresses complex problems in complex settings rather than simplified problems in isolation.
options: Simple, isolated settings with clear-cut answers
Complex settings with complex problems rather than simplified problems in isolation

questions.text: Service learning promotes the habit of critical thinking defined as:
questions.explanation: Service learning offers powerful opportunities to acquire the habit of critical thinking — the ability to identify the most important questions or issues within a real-world situation.
options: The ability to identify the most important questions or issues within a real-world situation

questions.text: Service learning is NOT about:
questions.explanation: Service learning is not about an episodic (occasional) volunteer program, though volunteering is an integral component of it.

questions.text: Service learning is NOT:
questions.explanation: Service learning is not only for university or college students; it is for all age groups.
options: Only for university or college students

questions.text: Service learning is NOT compensatory service assigned as:
questions.explanation: Service learning is not compensatory service assigned as a form of punishment by school management.

questions.text: The distinctive element of service learning is that it:
questions.explanation: The distinctive element is that service learning enhances the community through service, but also has powerful learning consequences for students and participating communities.
options: Benefits only students, not the community
Benefits only the community, not the students
Enhances the community through service AND has powerful learning consequences for students
Replaces all other forms of education

questions.text: One of the goals of service learning is to:
questions.explanation: One goal is to challenge the students' assumptions, enlarge their view of the world and invite them to further engage their intelligence and imagination.
options: Limit students' engagement with the outside world
Challenge students' assumptions and enlarge their view of the world

questions.text: Which of the following is a goal of service learning?
questions.explanation: One goal is to meet community identified needs and activate community partnerships.
options: To isolate students from the community
To meet community identified needs and activate community partnerships
To eliminate the role of faculty in education

questions.text: Service learning seeks to develop:
questions.explanation: One goal of service learning is to develop student leaders within the field of service learning.
options: Student leaders within the field of service learning
Students who focus only on personal success
Students who depend entirely on faculty

questions.text: Which of the following is a benefit of service learning to students?
questions.explanation: Service learning enhances students' understanding of the academic curriculum.
options: Reduces the need for academic study
Enhances their understanding of the academic curriculum

questions.text: Service learning fosters which civic responsibility among students?
questions.explanation: Service learning fosters civic responsibility and encourages community involvement among students.

questions.text: Service learning provides students with opportunity to:
questions.explanation: Service learning gives students the opportunity to interact with people of diverse cultures and lifestyles.
options: Avoid interaction with people of diverse cultures
Interact with people of diverse cultures and lifestyles
Focus only on their own cultural group

questions.text: What does service learning provide in terms of career development?
questions.explanation: Service learning provides valuable and competitive career exploration opportunities to students.
options: Valuable and competitive career exploration opportunities
Only academic knowledge with no practical application

questions.text: Service learning benefits faculty by:
questions.explanation: Service learning provides inspiration and invigoration of teaching methods among teachers.
options: Providing inspiration and invigoration of teaching methods

questions.text: Which of the following is a benefit of service learning to faculty/department?
questions.explanation: Service learning gives faculty opportunities to tap expertise of community agencies as co-teachers.
options: Opportunities to tap expertise of community agencies as co-teachers

questions.text: Service learning benefits the community by providing:
questions.explanation: The community benefits through access to institution's resources (both human and materials).
options: Access to institution's resources (both human and materials)
Free education for all community members

questions.text: How does service learning benefit the community in terms of employment?
questions.explanation: Service learning benefits the community through development of a pool of potential employees.
options: By development of a pool of potential employees

questions.text: Service learning bridges the gap between:
questions.explanation: One benefit to the community is bridging the gap between the government and the community.

questions.text: Service learning benefits the institution by:
questions.explanation: Service learning facilitates faculty and students' engagement issues as one of its institutional benefits.
options: Facilitating faculty and students' engagement issues
Eliminating the need for community outreach

questions.text: One of the institutional benefits of service learning is:
questions.explanation: Service learning benefits institutions by increasing development and preparation of graduates for future life challenges.
options: Increased development and preparation of graduates for future life challenges
Reducing the number of programs offered

questions.text: Which of the following is a component of service learning?
questions.explanation: Curricular connections are a key component — service learning involves integrating learning into a service project with clear academic ties.

questions.text: In community settings, 'Students' Voice' in service learning is alternatively called:
questions.explanation: Students' Voice, where students have opportunity to select, design, implement and evaluate their service activity, is alternatively called 'Youth voice' in community settings.

questions.text: Reflection as a component of service learning involves:
questions.explanation: Reflection involves structured opportunities for students to think, talk and write about their service experience.
options: Structural opportunities for students to think, talk and write about their service experience

questions.text: The 'balance of reflection and action' in service learning:
questions.explanation: The balance of reflection and action allows a student to constantly be aware of the impact of their work.
options: Allows a student to be constantly aware of the impact of their work

questions.text: Community Partnership as a component of service learning is used to:
questions.explanation: Community Partnership provides partnership with community agencies to identify genuine needs, provide mentorship and contribute assets towards completing projects.
options: Identify genuine needs, provide mentorship and contribute assets towards completing projects

questions.text: Authentic Community Needs as a component of service learning means:
questions.explanation: Authentic Community Needs means local community members or service recipients are involved in determining the significance and depth of service activities.
options: Faculty decides what the community needs
Local community members or service recipients are involved in determining the significance and depth of service activities

questions.text: The Assessment component of service learning provides:
questions.explanation: Well-structured assessment instruments with constructive feedback through reflection provide valuable information regarding positive 'reciprocal learning' and serving outcomes.
options: Valuable information regarding reciprocal learning and serving outcomes through structured instruments and constructive feedback
A method to rank students competitively

questions.text: Which type of service learning involves direct person-to-person, face-to-face projects such as tutoring?
questions.explanation: Direct Service Learning involves direct person-to-person, face-to-face projects in which service impacts individuals who receive direct help (tutoring, work with elderly, peer mediation, etc.).

questions.text: Indirect Service Learning includes projects that benefit:
questions.explanation: Indirect Service Learning benefits the community as opposed to specific individuals — examples include environmental, construction, restoration, food or clothing drives.
options: The community as opposed to specific individuals (environmental, construction, restoration projects)

questions.text: Advocacy Service Learning aims at:
questions.explanation: Advocacy Service Learning aims at working, acting, speaking, writing, presenting, informing — projects that encourage action or create awareness on issues of public interest.
options: Working, acting, speaking, writing, presenting to encourage action or create awareness on issues of public interest

questions.text: Research Service Learning includes:
questions.explanation: Research Service Learning includes surveys, studies, evaluation, experiments, data gathering, etc. to find, compile and report information on topics of public interest.
options: Surveys, studies, evaluation, experiments and data gathering to report information on topics of public interest

questions.text: Which type of service learning is exemplified by care for the environment, violence prevention and drug prevention awareness?
questions.explanation: Advocacy Service Learning includes projects that encourage action or create awareness on issues of public interest like care for the environment, violence, drug prevention, disaster preparedness, etc.

questions.text: Pure service learning courses are primarily focused on:
questions.explanation: Pure service learning courses have as their intellectual core the idea of service to communities. Students enroll because they are interested in volunteerism, student activism, and civic engagement.
options: Community service, volunteerism, student activism and civic engagement

questions.text: In discipline-based service learning, students:
questions.explanation: In discipline-based service learning, students are expected to serve in the community throughout the semester and reflect on their experiences regularly using course content as a basis for analysis.
options: Serve only once during the semester
Serve in the community throughout the semester and reflect regularly using course content as a basis for analysis
Only study theory in the classroom

questions.text: In Problem-Based Service Learning (PBSL), students relate to the community as:
questions.explanation: In PBSL, students relate to the community much as 'consultants' working for a 'client,' working to understand a specific community problem and develop solutions.

questions.text: Capstone courses in service learning are generally designed for:
questions.explanation: Capstone courses are generally designed for majors and minors in a given discipline and are offered almost exclusively to students in their final year.
options: Students in their final year (majors and minors in a given discipline)

questions.text: The goal of capstone courses in service learning is usually to:
questions.explanation: The goal of capstone courses is to synthesize students' understanding of their discipline and help students make the transition from the world of theory to the world of practice.
options: Introduce students to a new field completely
Synthesize students' understanding of their discipline and help transition from theory to practice
Replace community service with laboratory work

questions.text: Service internships differ from traditional internships primarily through:
questions.explanation: Service internships differ from traditional internships by their reflection component and focus on reciprocity — the idea that the community and the student benefit equally.
options: The reflection component and their focus on reciprocity

questions.text: How many hours per week do students typically work in service internships?
questions.explanation: In service internships, students typically work between 10 and 40 hours in the community setting.

questions.text: Community-based action research is similar to an independent study option appropriate for students who are:
questions.explanation: Community-based action research is appropriate for students with substantial experience in community service and adequate knowledge of research methodology.
options: New to community work with no prior experience
Highly experienced in community work with adequate knowledge of research methodology
In their first year of university

questions.text: Community needs in service learning refer to:
questions.explanation: Community needs are problems (unmet needs) that have been identified to hinder the growth and development of individual members as well as the community as a whole.
options: Only financial needs of the community
Problems (unmet needs) that hinder the growth and development of individual members and the community
The academic needs of students only

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of a community partner?
questions.explanation: Community partners include: public service agencies, non-profit organizations (Red Cross, CAN, JNI), governmental organizations (Ministries), and NGOs (Human Rights, Civil Societies).
options: Public service agencies, non-profit organizations, governmental and non-governmental organizations

questions.text: An example of a non-profit organization that can serve as a community partner is:
questions.explanation: Non-profit organizations such as Red Cross, CAN, and JNI are examples of community partners in service learning.

questions.text: Community partnership in service learning is beneficial because it:
questions.explanation: Service learning and community partnership facilitates multi-faceted learning opportunities by connecting educators and students with service providers, non-profit organizations and other community agencies.
options: Replaces the need for faculty involvement
Facilitates multi-faceted learning opportunities by connecting educators and students with community agencies
Reduces the academic workload of students
Eliminates the need for community service

questions.text: Community partnership helps build:
questions.explanation: Community partnership helps to build a shared sense of commitment and responsibility throughout the community, avoiding unnecessary duplication of efforts.
options: A shared sense of commitment and responsibility throughout the community

questions.text: The first step to establishing a successful community partnership is:
questions.explanation: The first step is identifying potential partners, which may include universities, NGOs, individuals, government, and recipients of services.
options: Identifying potential partners (universities, NGOs, individuals, government, recipients of services)

questions.text: Partnership can be established through Networking which involves:
questions.explanation: Networking involves sharing information with community agencies on your plan of activities.
options: Sharing of resources and realigning of activities
Sharing information with community agencies on your plan of activities
Sharing resources and information to enhance partner capacity
Scheduling joint activities with two or more agencies

questions.text: Coordination in community partnership involves:
questions.explanation: Coordination involves sharing information and scheduling of joint activities with two or more community agencies for mutual benefits.
options: Sharing information and scheduling of joint activities with two or more community agencies for mutual benefit
Sharing resources and enhancing partner capacity

questions.text: Collaboration in community partnership involves:
questions.explanation: Collaboration involves sharing resources and information with different community agencies to enhance the capacity of other partners for the mutual benefit of all.
options: Sharing information only with plan of activities
Sharing resources and information with different community agencies to enhance the capacity of other partners for mutual benefit
Sharing resources and realigning activities for mutual benefit

questions.text: Cooperation in community partnership involves:
questions.explanation: Cooperation involves sharing of resources, information and realigning of activities for the mutual benefit of all.
options: Sharing information with agencies on your plan of activities only
Sharing resources information and realigning of activities for mutual benefit of all
Sharing resources to enhance partner capacity

questions.text: Community partnership through service learning demonstrates that young people:
questions.explanation: Community partnership through service learning provides students and youth with increased confidence in their ability and shows that young people can make valuable contributions to change things for the better.
options: Can make valuable contributions to change things for the better (positive transformation)

questions.text: Volunteerism is defined as:
questions.explanation: Volunteerism is the practice of using volunteer workers especially in community service or educational organizations and programs.
options: The practice of using volunteer workers especially in community service or educational organizations and programs

questions.text: What distinguishes service learning from traditional volunteerism?
questions.explanation: Service learning is more than traditional volunteering because it combines service activities with structured reflections, fostering an ethic of civic responsibility.
options: Service learning does not involve community service
Service learning combines service activities with structured reflections
Volunteerism has more academic content than service learning
Service learning does not require student participation

questions.text: It is the ________ that distinguishes service learning from volunteerism.
questions.explanation: It is the reflection that distinguishes service learning from the concept of volunteerism because it is not an episodic (occasional) volunteer program.

questions.text: Volunteerism is said to be ________ of service learning.
questions.explanation: Volunteerism is said to be an integral part of service learning.

questions.text: Civic engagement is defined as:
questions.explanation: Civic engagement is the state of being meshed (coming together) into working arrangement relating to one's contribution to the community or country — becoming a good citizen.
options: The state of being involved in working arrangements relating to one's contribution to the community or country

questions.text: Examples of civic engagement/community action projects include:
questions.explanation: Examples of civic engagement/community action projects include college access weekend, environmental cleanliness, peace garden projects, and museum partnership.
options: College access weekend, environmental cleanliness, peace garden projects, museum partnership

questions.text: In service learning, action projects are designed to provide student leaders opportunities to:
questions.explanation: Action projects are designed to provide students' leaders an opportunity to develop and practice leadership skills relevant to service learning.
options: Develop and practice leadership skills relevant to service learning

questions.text: Leadership is defined as:
questions.explanation: Leadership is the ability to guide, direct or influence people.
options: The ability to guide, direct or influence people
The ability to pass academic examinations

questions.text: Service learning student leadership within the classroom acts as:
questions.explanation: Service learning students' leadership within the classroom acts as peer mentors and facilitators of reflection, helping fellow students to explore sensitive issues related to service and social justice.
options: Peer mentors and facilitators of reflection, helping fellow students explore sensitive issues

questions.text: Service learning student leadership provides support for which three constituencies?
questions.explanation: Service learning students' leadership provides available support for all three constituencies in the service learning process: faculty, community partners and students.

questions.text: Service learning helps facilitate the development of:
questions.explanation: Service learning students' leadership helps to facilitate the development of a community motivated for social change.
options: A community motivated for social change

questions.text: Youth Voice in service learning is:
questions.explanation: Youth Voice is the input/opinion of young people in developing and implementing policies, plans and projects to guide service learning efforts.
options: Only the opinion of faculty about youth
The input/opinion of young people in developing and implementing policies, plans and projects
Only the voices of adult community members

questions.text: Youth Voice benefits young people by:
questions.explanation: Youth Voice provides young people with increased self-esteem (confidence) and sense of personal control.
options: Providing increased self-esteem and sense of personal control
Keeping them away from organizational activities

questions.text: Youth Voice changes how adults view young people by:
questions.explanation: Youth Voice changes how adults view young people — they are likely to be viewed as critical to organizational improvement.
options: Keeping young people in subordinate roles
Making adults likely to view young people as critical to organizational improvement

questions.text: 'Youth as Trainers' in the models for engaging Youth Voice means:
questions.explanation: Youth as Trainers means well-trained youth are supported to design and deliver training about service learning or orientation for service learning projects.
options: Youth train adults on organizational management
Well-trained youth are supported to design and deliver training about service learning or orientation for service learning projects
Youth train other youth on sports
Youth are trained by corporate companies

questions.text: 'Youth as Planners' involves youth in:
questions.explanation: Youth as Planners means engaging youth in planning and implementing service projects — identifying objectives, recruiting volunteers, developing action plans, timelines and evaluating projects.
options: Planning and implementing service projects: identifying objectives, recruiting volunteers, developing action plans and evaluating projects

questions.text: 'Youth as Evaluators' involves youth in:
questions.explanation: Youth as Evaluators means youth assess program effectiveness by being involved in development and implementation of surveys, conducting interviews and documenting findings.
options: Assessing program effectiveness through surveys, interviews and documenting findings

questions.text: Youth Action/Advisory Councils (YAC) are:
questions.explanation: Youth Action/Advisory Councils (YAC) are groups of young people working with an existing organization to keep youth involved in the organization's mission — helping make decisions and address specific issues.
options: Groups of young people working with an existing organization to keep youth involved in the mission of the organization

questions.text: 'Youth Summits' provide young people with an opportunity to:
questions.explanation: Youth Summits bring young people together for discussion and action around issues important to them, providing them with an opportunity to voice their concerns and develop solutions.
options: Come together for discussion and action around issues important to them, voice concerns and develop solutions

questions.text: 'Youth as Funders' involves youth in:
questions.explanation: Youth as Funders involves youth's participation in philanthropy — raising money, developing request for proposals, reviewing proposals and determining who gets the money.
options: Philanthropy — raising money, developing proposals, reviewing proposals and determining who gets the money

questions.text: 'Youth on Board' means young people serving as:
questions.explanation: Youth on Board means young people on organizational governing structures, especially boards, as full voting members with all the same place in organizational decision making as other board members.
options: Junior observers with no voting rights
Full voting members on organizational governing structures/boards with the same decision-making rights as other members

questions.text: When preparing youth for decision/leadership roles, one should:
questions.explanation: To prepare youth for leadership roles, you should provide them with skills, tools and information they will need to be successful in the role identified.
options: Provide them with skills, tools and information they will need to be successful in the identified role
Limit their access to organizational information

questions.text: Academic service learning always involves:
questions.explanation: Academic service learning always involves some kind of formal involvement on the part of the University or its staff, unlike volunteering.
options: Some kind of formal involvement on the part of the university or its staff

questions.text: Service learning is almost always tied to:
questions.explanation: Service learning is almost always tied to a credit-bearing course, unlike volunteering.

questions.text: Service learning always includes:
questions.explanation: Service learning always includes critical reflection, which is one of the key differences from volunteerism.

questions.text: Volunteerism does NOT involve:
questions.explanation: Volunteerism does not involve a connection to a specific course and is designed for the benefit of recipients and community, without academic credit.
options: A connection to a specific course for academic credit

questions.text: Service learning meets which three sets of needs simultaneously?
questions.explanation: Service learning meets community needs, university needs and student learning needs simultaneously.
options: Community needs, university needs and student learning needs

questions.text: The Philanthropic Model of service learning is:
questions.explanation: The Philanthropic Model is based on the perceived need for charity and philanthropy. It claims neutrality regarding social issues and argues for altruism and compensatory justice.
options: Based on democracy and equal participation
Based on the perceived need for charity and philanthropy, claiming neutrality regarding social issues

questions.text: The Philanthropic Model is best applied in situations where:
questions.explanation: Philanthropic Model is a tool of mitigation or immediate relief, best applied in cases and situations where other models of service learning have not yet been employed or considered.
options: All other models have been tried and failed
Other models of service learning have not yet been employed or considered
Students are in their final year

questions.text: The Civic Engagement Model is based on the premise that:
questions.explanation: The Civic Engagement Model is based on the premise that democracy demands equal participation and voice of all citizens.
options: Humans are social beings who prioritize community
Democracy demands equal participation and voice of all citizens
Charity and philanthropy are the foundation of service
Individual egotism is the basis of social interaction

questions.text: The Communitarian Model assumes that:
questions.explanation: The Communitarian Model assumes that humans are social beings, not self-interested individual egotists. Service learning is central to developing a sense of human community at the local level.
options: Humans are self-interested individuals focused on liberty and property
Humans are social beings, not self-interested egotists, and service learning develops sense of community
Democracy is the only basis for civic action
Service learning should only benefit individuals

questions.text: The Civic Engagement Model renews the focus of higher education on:
questions.explanation: Civic engagement model renews and alters the focus of higher education institutions on service as the focal point of their mission of teaching, research, and professional service.
options: Service as the focal point of their mission of teaching, research and professional service

questions.text: The reflection process in service learning takes place:
questions.explanation: The reflection process in service learning takes place before, during and after projects.

questions.text: Pre-service (before) reflection includes:
questions.explanation: Pre-service reflection includes: identifying a project, increasing awareness of important community issues, planning/preparation and imagining potential problems and possible solutions.
options: Identifying a project, increasing awareness of community issues, planning and imagining potential problems

questions.text: During service, observation in reflection involves:
questions.explanation: During service, observation involves guidance to describe the projects in their social context, personal reaction, etc.
options: Guidance to describe the project in its social context, including personal reaction

questions.text: Post-service reflection helps students to:
questions.explanation: Post-service reflection helps to further analyze current situations, assess accomplishments, promote increased sense of self-awareness, and evaluate the accomplishment of learning goals.
options: Further analyze situations, assess accomplishments, promote self-awareness and evaluate learning

questions.text: Reflection is described as 'the glue that holds service and learning together to provide':
questions.explanation: Reflection is the glue that holds service and learning together to provide optimal educative experiences.

questions.text: Reflection in service learning leads to students':
questions.explanation: Reflection leads to students' new ideas and is crucial for integrating service experience with course material, enhancing critical understanding.
options: New ideas and enhanced critical understanding of course topics

questions.text: Successful reflection must be 'Continuous', meaning it:
questions.explanation: Reflection must be Continuous — it must take place before, during and after the completion of the service project to be fully useful.
options: Only occurs once after the project
Must take place before, during and after the completion of the service project

questions.text: Successful reflection must be 'Challenging', meaning it:
questions.explanation: Challenging reflection involves pushing ourselves out of our comfort zones to make new connections between concepts and to think in new ways.
options: Must be easy and comfortable for students
Involves pushing ourselves out of comfort zones to make new connections between concepts and think in new ways

questions.text: Successful reflection must be 'Contextualized', meaning it is:
questions.explanation: Contextualized reflection is framed in a manner that is appropriate for the context in which the service experience takes place.
options: Framed in a manner appropriate for the context in which the service experience takes place
The same regardless of the service environment

questions.text: Successful reflection can serve as a bridge between:
questions.explanation: Successful reflection can serve as a bridge between the service connected experience and our discipline-based academic knowledge.
options: The service-connected experience and discipline-based academic knowledge

questions.text: Which of the following is a best tip for successful reflection experience?
questions.explanation: Best tips for successful reflection include: be attentive to and mindful of the present moment.
options: Be attentive to and mindful of the present moment

questions.text: When reflecting, you should:
questions.explanation: A best tip for reflection is to use the lens of your past experiences to make links to the present.
options: Use the lens of your past experiences to make links to the present

questions.text: Service learning projects can be funded through which of the following?
questions.explanation: Service learning projects can be funded through students' contributions, grants from individual community members, donations from NGOs, foundations and contributions from community partners.
options: Students' contributions, grants, donations from NGOs, foundations and community partners

questions.text: Funds raised for service learning projects should be:
questions.explanation: Funds raised for every project should be used for the identified project and properly accounted for at the end of the project.
options: Used for any purpose the students choose
Used for the identified project and properly accounted for at the end of the project
Deposited in a bank account indefinitely

questions.text: All service learning projects should be executed within:
questions.explanation: All projects identified and initiated should be executed within stipulated timelines and reports written and copied to all stakeholders and partners.
options: Stipulated timelines with reports written and copied to all stakeholders and partners
A period of exactly one year

questions.text: Evaluation of service learning projects should be done to:
questions.explanation: Evaluation of all projects should be done to update progress and identify any need for adjustments.
options: Update progress and identify any need for adjustments

questions.text: Service learning presents which type of experience for students and lecturers?
questions.explanation: Service learning presents unique and enriched learning and personal growth experiences for students and lecturers while strengthening communities by addressing unmet community needs.
options: Unique and enriched learning and personal growth experiences while strengthening communities

questions.text: Service learning is described as a dynamic process through which students':
questions.explanation: Service learning is a dynamic process through which students' personal and social growth is tightly interwoven into their academic and cognitive development.
options: Personal and social growth is tightly interwoven with their academic and cognitive development

questions.text: Service learning draws on multiple knowledge sources which include:
questions.explanation: Service learning as a teaching method draws on multiple knowledge sources: academic, students' knowledge and experience, and community knowledge.
options: Academic knowledge, students' knowledge and experience, and community knowledge

questions.text: Service learning is more likely to be personally meaningful because:
questions.explanation: Service learning promotes deeper learning because the results are immediate and uncontrived, making it more likely to be personally meaningful and generate emotional consequence, challenging values and ideas.
options: The results are immediate and uncontrived, generating emotional consequences and challenging values
It is easy and requires no effort

questions.text: Service learning seeks to disseminate models of service learning excellence to:
questions.explanation: One goal is to disseminate models of service learning excellence to stakeholders within and beyond the institution's community.
options: Stakeholders within and beyond the institution's community

questions.text: Service learning provides diverse and practical experiences in:
questions.explanation: Service learning provides diverse and practical experiences in real world situations.

questions.text: Service learning raises awareness of:
questions.explanation: Service learning raises awareness of social justice issues among students.

questions.text: Service learning connects community with curriculum and makes faculty more aware of:
questions.explanation: Service learning connects the community with curriculum and makes faculty more aware of current social issues as they relate to academic areas of interest.
options: Current social issues as they relate to academic areas of interest

questions.text: Service learning provides the community with short and long term solutions to:
questions.explanation: Service learning provides short and long term solutions to pressing community needs and problems.

questions.text: Students' Discussion as a component of service learning includes:
questions.explanation: Students' Discussion involves the opportunity to discuss their learning experiences in class discussion and includes the use of social networks.
options: Discussion of learning experiences in class and the use of social networks

questions.text: Tutoring and working with the elderly are examples of which type of service learning?
questions.explanation: Tutoring, work with the elderly, oral histories, and peer mediation are examples of Direct Service Learning — direct person-to-person, face-to-face projects.

questions.text: Water testing and energy surveys are examples of which type of service learning?
questions.explanation: Water testing, energy surveys, and studies on public buildings are examples of Research Service Learning.

questions.text: The academic purpose of pure service learning courses is to:
questions.explanation: The academic purpose of pure service learning courses is to prepare students for active and informed civic participation.
options: Prepare students for professional careers only
Prepare students for active and informed civic participation

questions.text: In PBSL, the final product delivered to the community represents:
